newsitem.title: UK: BA plane crash-lands on two wheels, all escape.
newsitem.headline: BA plane crash-lands on two wheels, all escape.

text.p: A British Airways regional airliner on Sunday made a dramatic crash landing on two wheels after the left undercarriage failed, but all 70 people on board escaped without serious injury, officials said.

An airport spokesman said the British Aerospace ATP airliner had just taken off from Manchester at 7 p.m. (1800 GMT) when the captain realised the left undercarriage had locked in the upright position.

He immediately declared an emergency and the plane, which had been heading for Knock in Ireland, ditched fuel before coming back into Manchester airport to land at 8.05 p.m. (1905 GMT) with just the nose and right wheels working.
The pilot managed to keep the plane upright until his speed dropped and the left wing hit the ground, starting a small blaze which was quickly put out by fire engines pursuing the airliner.
"The pilot did an excellent job. There were 63 passengers on board, but there was not a single casualty," the spokesman told the domestic Press Association news agency.
Those on board the plane escaped using emergency slides. A spokesman for the ambulance service said two of those on board were treated for minor cuts.
Manchester airport was closed for the crash landing, rescue operation and removal of the plane from the runway.
The airliner was operated on behalf of BA by British Regional Airlines, based on the Isle of Man.
"In the circumstances it was an excellent handling of the airliner," British Regional Airlines director Michael Bathgate told Sky television news.
A British Airways spokeswoman contacted by telephone said she could not immediately comment since she was still collecting information on the incident.
